facts.name: Hosta
facts.color: Lavender or white spikes; grown for leaves
facts.notes: Bold leaves in every shade of green, blue and gold. The backbone of many shade gardens. Deer and slugs love it too.

fall.why: dead hosta leaves hide slug eggs, so rake them all up

sources.title: Penn State Extension: Cutting Down Perennials in the Fall
sources.note: Cut peonies, daylilies, brunnera and speedwell in fall; cut bee balm and garden phlox with powdery mildew and destroy the leaves; rake up hosta leaves (slug eggs); cut yarrow and Shasta daisy flower stalks but keep the base leaves. Leave grasses, Siberian iris, baptisia, sedum, Joe-Pye weed, coneflower, black-eyed Susan and most natives standing; leave marginally hardy anise hyssop tops over winter; tidy hardy geraniums, heucheras, hellebores and moss phlox in spring.

sources.title: University of Minnesota Extension: Dividing Perennials
sources.note: Divide fall bloomers in spring and spring and summer bloomers in fall, 4 to 6 weeks before the ground freezes; peonies and Siberian iris in fall; hostas in spring; avoid dividing baptisia.
